item.description: Ivar Stenberg , through 12 games, has been terrific on the power play. He’s still a significant work in progress at 5-on-5. There’s nothing wrong with that: The San Jose Sharks winger is a 19-year-old rookie battling through his D+1 draft year in the best league in the world. It’s something special that Stenberg has even excelled on the power play, where he’s piled up seven of his nine points. Most teens wouldn’t be any good at any facet of the NHL, especially not something as important as top power play unit duty. Per Stathletes , here’s what’s been truly impressive about Stenberg on the PP, and what he’s got to work on at 5-on-5. Plays Under Pressure Here’s why Stenberg may not leave the San Jose Sharks top power play unit any time soon. To the eye, he’s been cool as a cucumber with the puck, veteran-like with the extra space afforded, up a man. “He’s so calm and he’s so confident with the puck, so it doesn’t matter if he’s getting pressured hard,” Macklin Celebrini said. “If he has a little bit of time and space, he’s always able to make that play.” He actually leads the San Jose Sharks with 50.91 Plays Under Pressure Per 60 on the power play. item.title: Hillsdale Academy soccer reaches first regional title game since 2020
item.description: YPSILANTI — Hillsdale Academy boys soccer is one victory away from breaking through a postseason barrier that has stood in the way of the Colts throughout their historic run of district championships this decade. More: Hillsdale Academy coach Neal Brady earns 300th win The Colts advanced to the Division 4, Region 15 championship game with an 8-0 shutout victory over Ypsilanti Arbor Prep at Ypsilanti Lincoln High School. The victory improved Hillsdale Academy to 15-3-2 overall and gave longtime head coach Neal Brady his 301st career win, just four days after the Colts celebrated his milestone 300th victory alongside their seventh consecutive district championship. Senior Justin Busby led the offensive charge with five goals, continuing his impressive postseason performance after scoring the game-winner in double overtime against Jackson Christian in Friday’s district championship game. Busby opened the scoring against Arbor Prep on an assist from Danny Rodriguez. The senior went on to find the back of the net four more times as the Colts overwhelmed the Gators. Other goal scorers included Rodriguez, Symeon Jackson and Micah Diener, helping Hillsdale Academy secure another dominant shutout victory in the state tournament. This was the 13th shutout of the season for the Colts behind impressive play from its defensive play and junior goalkeeper Robert Whalen. For the Colts, the convincing victory sets the stage for what could be one of the most important games in the program’s recent history. Despite winning seven straight district championships, Hillsdale Academy has been unable to break through at the regional level. The Colts last played for a regional championship in 2020, when they fell to eventual Division 4 state champion Adrian Lenawee Christian. Now, six years later, Hillsdale Academy will have another opportunity to add a regional trophy to its growing collection. However, standing in the way will be a familiar postseason adversary. Colts set for another regional showdown with University Liggett Hillsdale Academy will face Grosse Pointe Woods University Liggett in the Division 4, Region 15 championship game at 6 p.m. Thursday, Oct. 29, at Ypsilanti Lincoln High School. The Knights advanced with a 4-0 shutout victory over Allen Park Inter-City Baptist in Tuesday’s opening semifinal, setting up another postseason meeting between two programs that have become well acquainted over the years. University Liggett enters the championship game undefeated at 19-0 and has yet to allow a goal during its postseason run. The Knights defeated Hillsdale Academy 3-1 in the regular-season meeting Aug. 21 at Hayden Park, but the history between the two programs extends well beyond this year’s matchup. In 2021, University Liggett eliminated Hillsdale Academy in a heartbreaking 3-2 regional semifinal decided in a shootout on a cold October night. item.title: "This is where I want to be": Riley answers the noise head-on
item.description: LOS ANGELES --- USC 's offense enters its biggest home game of the season carrying the weight of its ugliest performance in quite some time. A 24-7 upset loss at unranked Wisconsin has reignited every question about Lincoln Riley's job security in the process. Riley didn't dodge it Tuesday, addressing his standing with the program directly. "This is where I want to be," he said. "This is the right place for me. I'm the right person to be here, and that's as honest and transparent as I can be." Riley also addressed speculation about his relationship with USC leadership, particularly athletic director Jen Cohen, calling it stronger than the chatter suggests. "She's a tremendous AD. Even though she's not the AD that I came here with and I'm not the head coach that she hired...fantastic relationship. She's been a huge part of all the progress that we've made." On the performance itself against Wisconsin, Riley was self-critical about his own play-calling, particularly in the second half. The Trojans finished the night with a miserable -17 rushing yards, putting up their lowest point total since 2018. "The biggest problem I thought was I didn't do a good enough job staying with it to be completely honest," he said of his run game. "We could have been better, which always for a playcaller is going to increase your confidence to call it more." That same self-accountability was a theme for the rest of the offense on Tuesday. Quarterback Jayden Maiava, who threw two interceptions in the loss, put the result squarely on himself rather than the circumstances around him. "Just didn't play to my standard, and the Trojan standard," he said. "Got to play better. Can't dwell on that. Another big opponent coming up this weekend." Maiava also pointed to his teammates picking him up - literally, in the form of Justin Tauanuu, after his second interception - as evidence of a locker room that's looking to tighten instead of fray under the outside scrutiny. "That just shows the kind of team that there is right now. After a tough loss like that on the road, we just buy in more to each other." Running back King Miller echoed that same refusal to let frustration splinter the group, crediting backup Shahn Alston's readiness when called upon as proof of the program's depth holding up even in a loss. Alston led all Trojan rushers with 28 yards on seven carries. "He's shown it all since spring, since he's been here," Miller said. "He's one of the guys that studies his tail off, recovers his body. When you put him out there, I had no doubt he was going to do exactly what he was supposed to." With Ohio State having allowed just 650 rushing yards from opponents this season (fourth-least in the Big Ten), the job won't get any easier for Miller, Alston or the rest of the running back room as they look to bounce back. item.title: Seahawks make roster move to clear space for Quenton Nelson on offensive line
item.description: © Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Seahawks make roster move to clear space for Quenton Nelson on offensive line appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In a blockbuster move on Tuesday, the Seattle Seahawks acquired veteran offensive lineman Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection. The trade is contingent on Nelson passing a physical. To make room for their newest addition on the 53-man roster, Seattle waived guard Christian Haynes. Nelson arrives with an impressive resume, having earned Pro Bowl recognition in each of his eight NFL seasons and collecting six All-Pro selections, including three first-team honors. His addition gives the Seahawks an experienced option to strengthen an offensive line that has left much to be desired in the run game and surrendered 14 sacks of quarterback Sam Darnold across six games. Haynes, meanwhile, leaves Seattle after being unable to establish himself as a consistent starter since the Seahawks selected him 81st overall in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of UConn. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 2026 season offered the 25-year-old an opportunity to contribute more regularly. He made five starts during Anthony Bradford’s absence due to hip and knee injuries, logging 210 offensive snaps, all at right guard. Haynes had appeared in 31 games for Seattle, although he was unable to earn a permanent starting role during his first two campaigns. Bradford’s return in Week 7, coupled with the team’s recent additions along the interior offensive line, further clouded Haynes’ outlook. The Seahawks selected Grey Zabel in the first round of the 2025 draft and added fifth-round rookie Beau Stephens in 2026. The team also had Olu Oluwatimi available as interior line depth. Haynes’ departure does not necessarily end his time with the organization. He could return to Seattle’s practice squad if he clears waivers, with the organization having created an additional opening by releasing tight end Josiah Deguara from its practice squad. The Seahawks will now look to integrate Nelson into their offensive line as they attempt to address their woes up front. Nelson has primarily played left guard throughout his NFL career, the same position occupied by Zabel in Seattle, leaving the team with a decision to make regarding its interior offensive line alignment. item.title: Monroe County Region high school sports roundup for Tuesday, Oct. 27
item.description: NEW BOSTON – Matt Livindini called it “the toughest Regional in the state.” The New Boston Huron boys soccer coach may have a point. His team is hosting a Division 2 tourney that includes four state-ranked teams – Warren De La Salle (No. 6), University of Detroit Jesuit (9, Huron (12) and Dearborn Divine Child (14). “There’s a good chance that the state champion will come out of this Regional,” Lividini said. More: Takeaways from Monroe County Region football games in Week 9 Unfortunately for Lividini, that champion will not be Huron. The Chiefs opened the Regional with a 2-1 overtime loss to Divine Child on Tuesday, Oct. 27. “There is no sadness here,” Lividini said. “That’s the way is goes when two good teams play. It was an overtime game.” Huron had made it this far in the state tournament before, but had never been so competitive. “Our guys played well all night,” Lividini said. “There ever was a time when they did not want it.” Huron opened the scoring at the 19:12 mark of the first half when Matthew Hussey scored off a free kick following a hand ball in the goal box. Divine Child tied the game on a goal by Evan Scirri at the 30:19 mark of the second half. Neither team could score again until Mason Fraley headed in a ball in front of the net. Huron finishes with a 16-4-3 record despite returning only two starters from 2025. “I didn’t expect it right for the start, but these guys had a chip on their shoulders,” Lividini said. The Chiefs will lose just four players to graduation. “At the end tonight, I had two freshmen and four sophomores on the field,” Lividini said. PREP VOLLEYBALL Whiteford charges back OTTAWA LAKE – Whiteford roared back after dropping the first two sets to beat Erie Mason 26-24, 26-24, 21-25, 17-25, 15-5 Tuesday. Zoie Stubleski led Mason with 35 digs. Addie Homrich recorded 14 kills, Kaylee Wright 20 assists and Aubrey Iocoangeli 8 aces. Other leaders were Anna Gray (17 kills), Olivia Eby (58 assists) and Kiersten Soss (22 digs). item.title: Packers Coach LaFleur Hints At Parsons Return After Months Of Silence
item.description: Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) checks on defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (98) as Hargrave is carted off the field with an injury against the Chicago Bears on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers won the game, 31-7. Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur finally admitted a chance exists for Micah Parsons to return to practice soon. This comes more than 10 months after the star edge rusher tore his left knee on December 14. For weeks, the answer was a flat refusal, but the tone shifted on Tuesday. LaFleur told reporters, “I sure hope so,” marking a stark change from his previous hard no. The medical staff holds the final say on when Parsons can step back onto the field. LaFleur made his feelings clear while speaking to the press. That medical [decision] is what matters when the day concludes. Yeah, I’m itching [for] it, though, for sure, he said. He added simply, according to ESPN , “I’m saying there’s a chance.” Parsons tore his ACL and meniscus just before Christmas and had surgery two weeks later. A Shift in Practice Plans Parsons remains on the physically unable to perform list, which keeps him out of regular games. Once a player on this list returns to practice, the team has only three weeks to decide his roster spot. If the Packers bring him in next week, they must either keep him or place him on injured reserve by the deadline. The Packers face the Panthers on Thursday, so they will not hold regular practices this week. After a trip to New England on November 8, Green Bay hosts the Vikings in Week 10. The team then takes a bye in Week 11. This timeline suggests the first real game action for Parsons could be the first post-bye game on November 25 against the Rams. LaFleur acknowledged that his recent answer was different from the past month and a half. He knows the team needs his pass rush, but health comes first. The coach has faced this question weekly for six weeks. Parsons has done the hard work of recovery, but he still needs medical clearance. The team will see if his knee can handle NFL speed. Another Star Finds His Way Back While Parsons waits for the knee, Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat has already returned to the field. Sweat served a two-game suspension for taking a banned substance by accident. One day after Chicago beat New England, he was reinstated on October 23. He will play in Week 8 when the Bears face the Seahawks on Monday Night Football. Sweat described the time away as “devastating” to his reputation and his team. “It was a surprise. But you take a lick on the chin and keep moving forward,” Sweat said, according to ESPN . Missing those two games caused him to forfeit $2.3 million of his 2026 base salary. Sweat signed a four-year, $98 million deal when he joined the Bears in 2023. He had 12.5 sacks that season between Washington and Chicago. item.title: Zeeland barely holds off Holland Christian in battle of state swimming powers
item.description: The Zeeland girls swim team held off Holland Christian 95-91 in a battle of two of the top teams in the state. Zeeland is ranked No. 8 in Division 1, while Holland Christian is No. 3 in Division 3. Zeeland's Natalie Lauritzen, Ariyah Gettings, Mallory Ensing and Elsie Kapenga won the 200-yard medley relay in 1:50.96, holding off the Maroons 1:52.58). Zeeland went 1-2-3 in the 200 IM. Lauritzen won the race in 2:13.79, ahead of Ensing (2:17.51) and Skyla Gettings (2:26.05). Ariyah Gettings won the 200 freestyle in 2:00.56 as Zeeland nearly went 1-2. Defending state champion Camryn Siegers won the race in 23.57, while teammate Eliana Jernigan was second in 25.85. Siegers, also the defending state champion in the 100 backstroke, won that event in 55.79 over Lauritzen (59.38), who was all-state last year. item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Matt Hagan holds a 98-point lead over Jordan Vandergriff with only two races remaining in the season. This massive gap makes a fifth world title highly probable for the Funny Car driver. He has won four races and reached the final round seven times in 18 events. This weekend, The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway hosts the race. It is the 19th event on the 20-race schedule for the NHRA Mission Foods Drag Racing Series. Hagan drives a 12,000-horsepower Dodge//SRT Hellcat Funny Car. His team, Tony Stewart Racing, has been flawless so far. They have lost only two first-round races all year. The Math Behind the Championship He sits 119 points ahead of Dallas Glenn, the winner from the event in Dallas. Even if Hagan loses every remaining race, he would need a massive collapse to drop from first. The points system rewards consistency, and Hagan has delivered it every single week. His record includes three final-round appearances in the Countdown to the Championship playoff races. One of those wins came in Rockingham. The other event in the playoffs saw him finish in the semifinals. These results show he can perform when the pressure is highest. The data from these tracks is what he will use to close out the season. Vegas History and Team Goals Hagan has a strong history at this specific track. He is the defending event winner in Las Vegas. The city and the race have been very kind to his team in the past. He knows the data from this track better than most because he has won here before. That familiarity gives his team a clear edge for the weekend. The crew chief, Mike Knudsen, is chasing his first championship. Julian Champagnie has already made a habit of rewriting the San Antonio Spurs ’ record book from beyond the arc, and he did it again on Tuesday night against the Sacramento Kings. Champagnie drilled eight 3-pointers in the first half at Frost Bank Center, tying his own franchise record for made threes in a half. The forward was nearly perfect, going 8-of-10 from deep and scoring all 24 of his first-half points from long range. Julian Champagnie connects on his 8TH THREE of the first half, tying his own Spurs record for made threes in a half 😱 pic.twitter.com/1He93Eh0zu https://t.co/pL66kdjqpj Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 28, 2026 His barrage helped the Spurs pour in 80 points before the break and take an 80-54 lead into halftime. Victor Wembanyama added 23 points on 11-of-18 shooting to go with nine rebounds and two blocks, while second-year guard Dylan Harper chipped in nine points and five rebounds. Each Pro Bowl lineman was a cornerstone in the middle of their respective line’s trenches and were consistently among their unit’s best players in Indianapolis during their standout tenures. It was a tough day for the franchise, seeing highly regarded leaders and franchise mainstays leave their locker room for the final time, but one, that at least in some regards, was arguably necessary in the hopes of finding better days ahead for the Horseshoe. Let’s take a look at each trade and recap my initial reaction: Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks Trade Return: Seahawks’ 2027 3rd round pick and 2028 4th round pick This move wasn’t totally unexpected given where the Colts sit at 2-5, and much closer to now a full-on rebuild than title contention, but I’m a little surprised that: 1) Big Q was the first domino to fall regarding the fire sale, and 2) that Indianapolis moved him despite only receiving a 2027 3rd round pick and a future 4th rounder. Yes, I know that the 3rd round pick was “ unprecedented value for a Pro Bowl guard ,” but I just don’t see that return being all that meaningful for a perennial NFL All-Pro guard, future Hall of Famer, and homegrown Colts’ Ring of Honor candidate, who projects to have at least 3-4 elite years of football left in him at starting left guard. The Colts would be lucky to find a high-impact starter with a late 3rd round pick (as Seattle should be pretty good for the remainder of this season), that would match the 3-4 seasons of Hall of Fame guard play they would’ve received had they just kept Nelson on a lucrative, long-term deal extension that would’ve set the market again. We’ve seen other future Hall of Fame guards age rather gracefully until their mid-thirties too. Not saying it’s an exact science for Nelson by any means, but I don’t see any reason why he can’t have at least a handful of high level years still left in him.
